title: Simultaneous CRT coordinates for reduced root and idempotent-lift multiplication matrices
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal with nonzero R=A/I, f in A[X] monic, and g,h in R[X] monic and coprime with fbar=g*h. Let e in AdjoinRoot f have images 1 and 0 in AdjoinRoot g and AdjoinRoot h under the canonical coefficient-reduction quotient maps. Let T,P be multiplication by the root and by e in the power basis of AdjoinRoot f, and Tg,Th the root multiplication matrices in the power bases of AdjoinRoot g and AdjoinRoot h [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. There exist an index equivalence d: Fin deg f ≃ Fin deg g ⊕ Fin deg h and an invertible matrix U over R on this sum index such that U reindex_d(Tbar) U^-1 = blockdiag(Tg,Th) and U reindex_d(Pbar) U^-1 = blockdiag(1,0).

lean.statement: theorem adjoinRoot_crt_matrix {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [Nontrivial (A ⧸ I)] (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (g h : (A ⧸ I)[X]) (hg : g.Monic) (hh : h.Monic) (hcoprime : IsCoprime g h) (hfactor : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g * h) (e : AdjoinRoot f) (he₁ : AdjoinRoot.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f g (hfactor.symm ▸ dvd_mul_right g h) e = 1) (he₀ : AdjoinRoot.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f h (hfactor.symm ▸ dvd_mul_left h g) e = 0) : let b := (AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' hf).basis; let T := Algebra.leftMulMatrix b (AdjoinRoot.root f); let P := Algebra.leftMulMatrix b e; let Tg := Algebra.leftMulMatrix (AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' hg).basis (AdjoinRoot.root g); let Th := Algebra.leftMulMatrix (AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' hh).basis (AdjoinRoot.root h); ∃ (d : Fin f.natDegree ≃ (Fin g.natDegree ⊕ Fin h.natDegree)) (U : (Matrix (Fin g.natDegree ⊕ Fin h.natDegree) (Fin g.natDegree ⊕ Fin h.natDegree) (A ⧸ I))ˣ), U.val * Matrix.reindex d d (T.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) * U⁻¹.val = Matrix.fromBlocks Tg 0 0 Th ∧ U.val * Matrix.reindex d d (P.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) * U⁻¹.val = Matrix.fromBlocks 1 0 0 0

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal with $R=A/I\neq0$, $f\in A[X]$ monic, and $g,h\in R[X]$ monic and coprime with $\bar f=gh$, where $\bar f$ is the reduction of $f$ modulo $I$. Let $e\in A[X]/(f)$ have images $1$ in $R[X]/(g)$ and $0$ in $R[X]/(h)$ under the canonical coefficient-reduction quotient maps. Let $T,P$ be the matrices of multiplication by the class of $X$ and by $e$ on $A[X]/(f)$ in its power basis $1,X,\dots,X^{\deg f-1}$, and $T_g,T_h$ the matrices of multiplication by the class of $X$ on $R[X]/(g)$ and $R[X]/(h)$ in their power bases. There exist a bijection $d:\{0,\dots,\deg f-1\}\cong\{0,\dots,\deg g-1\}\sqcup\{0,\dots,\deg h-1\}$ and an invertible matrix $U$ over $R$ indexed by this disjoint union such that, writing $d_*$ for reindexing rows and columns along $d$ and $\bar T,\bar P$ for the reductions modulo $I$,
$$U\,d_*(\bar T)\,U^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}T_g&0\\0&T_h\end{pmatrix},\qquad U\,d_*(\bar P)\,U^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}.$$

proof.text: Let R=A/I, assumed nonzero. Monicity preserves the degree of f under coefficient reduction. The coordinates of the power basis of $A[X]/(f)$ reduce to the power basis of $R[X]/(\bar f)$. Multiplication matrices reduce entrywise: products of representatives are computed by division by the monic polynomial, and division and remainder commute with coefficient reduction. This follows by uniqueness of remainder and reducing the monic division identity.

For $\bar f=gh$, coprimality gives comaximal ideals (g) and (h). The Chinese remainder theorem gives the algebra isomorphism $R[X]/(\bar f)$ to $R[X]/(g)$ times $R[X]/(h)$. The two components are the quotient maps, so the root maps to the pair of roots and the residue of e maps to (1,0).

Concatenate the power bases of the two factors. Monicity over nonzero R gives $\deg f=\deg g+\deg h$. Hence their sum index type is equivalent to $\{0,\dots,\deg f-1\}$. Reindex the reduced basis along this equivalence d. The coordinate isomorphism to the concatenated basis is invertible; its matrix is a unit U. Its inverse is the inverse coordinate map, and their matrix products are identities since matrices of composites are products of matrices.

The CRT algebra equivalence intertwines multiplication. Multiplication by the pair of roots is block diagonal with the respective root matrices. Multiplication by (1,0) is the first projection with blocks 1,0,0,0. Applying the matrix-of-composition identity gives both conjugation identities with the same U. Degree-zero factors have the empty power basis, so no nontriviality assumption on either factor algebra is needed.
